Chapter 5: Building Motivation—Strategies to Increase Value and Expectancy.
Now that we've peeled back the layers behind procrastination, let's talk about what it really takes to get yourself moving. Motivation isn't just something you either have or you don't—it's something you can build. And the secret? It's all about increasing the value you see in a task, and your belief that you can actually pull it off.
So, let’s start with increasing value.
Think about this: if a task feels meaningful, or even just a little more fun, you’re way more likely to dive in. One way to do this is by connecting what you’re working on to your bigger goals. Maybe that report isn’t just paperwork—it’s a step toward your next job, or a chance to show what you’re really capable of. Or, you can make the work itself more enjoyable. Try listening to your favorite playlist while tackling something dull, or turn it into a friendly competition—even if you’re just racing the clock.
Here’s another trick: visualize the good stuff that comes from finishing. Picture the relief you’ll feel, the pride, or the new doors that might open once you’re done. Now, let’s talk about boosting expectancy—that’s your confidence that you’ll actually finish the job.
Breaking big tasks into smaller steps is a game-changer. Each small win builds your momentum, and you start to feel more capable with every step. Don’t be afraid to ask for feedback or support, either. Sometimes just talking things through with someone can clear up confusion or give you the encouragement you need. And when you’re doubting yourself, take a moment to remember other times you’ve faced something tough—and made it through.
When you combine these strategies, suddenly even the biggest tasks start to feel possible. Imagine someone who’s putting off writing a big report. They could start by jotting down just the main points—that’s a small step. Then, maybe bounce ideas off a coworker for support. And, most importantly, remind themselves of all the successful projects they’ve completed before. When a task feels both valuable and achievable, motivation starts to show up naturally.
It also helps to plan ahead for any obstacles. If you know distractions are an issue, set up your workspace to keep interruptions at bay. And if your energy dips after a while, schedule in breaks or little rewards to keep things fresh.
Here’s something to remember: building motivation isn’t about forcing yourself to work with pure willpower. It’s about making it easy—and even rewarding—to take action. When you focus on value and expectancy, and create an environment that helps you move forward, turning intentions into accomplishments really does become a step-by-step process.
